42constexpr std::string_view kRootPrefix = "//";
43constexpr std::string_view kTagPrefix = "@";
44constexpr std::string_view kRootMarkerFile = ".superdex_root";
45constexpr std::string_view kBotExtension = ".superdex_bot";
46constexpr std::string_view kBotSceneExtension = ".mochi_bot_scene";
47constexpr std::string_view kBotTaskExtension = ".mochi_bot_task";
48constexpr std::string_view kUrdfExtension = ".urdf";
49constexpr std::string_view kMjcfExtension = ".xml";
50constexpr std::string_view kCollisionSubdir = "collision";
51constexpr std::string_view kRenderSubdir = "render";
52constexpr std::string_view kCadSubdir = "cad";
53constexpr std::string_view kIntermediatesSubdir = "intermediates";
54
55/* The standard role folders, which sit side by side inside an asset's base folder (the folder
56 * holding its `.superdex_bot` / prefab file). Fixed order, so a search that sweeps them is
57 * deterministic. */
58constexpr std::array<std::string_view, 4> kAssetRoleSubdirs = {
59 kCadSubdir,
60 kCollisionSubdir,
61 kRenderSubdir,
62 kIntermediatesSubdir};
63
64/* Bot file references are descendant-only: a file-relative path may not ascend into a parent
65 * directory. Pass this as the maxParentDepth argument to @ref ResolveBotPath / @ref
66 * UnresolveBotPath / @ref MakePathRelative / @ref MakePathAbsolute for all bot (de)serialization.
67 * (Callers that store loosely-coupled local clusters, e.g. Studio's .StudioProcessing pipelines,
68 * opt into a small positive depth instead.) */
69constexpr int kBotPathMaxParentDepth = 0;

72// Asset folder layout

75/**
76 * @brief How one asset's files are arranged relative to its base folder.
77 */
78enum class AssetFolderLayout {
79 /// Models live in @ref kAssetRoleSubdirs children of the base folder.
80 RoleSubdirs,
81 /// Models live directly in the base folder, alongside the bot / prefab file.
82 Flat,
83};
84
85/**
86 * @brief Case-insensitive string equality.
87 *
88 * The asset layout is compared this way throughout -- role folder names here, asset base names in
89 * Studio's discovery -- so that a tree authored on a case-insensitive filesystem resolves the same
90 * way on a case-sensitive one.
91 */
92[[nodiscard]] inline bool EqualsCaseInsensitive(std::string_view a, std::string_view b) {
93 return std::equal(a.begin(), a.end(), b.begin(), b.end(), [](unsigned char x, unsigned char y) {
94 return std::tolower(x) == std::tolower(y);
95 });
96}

98/**
99 * @brief True if @p name is one of @ref kAssetRoleSubdirs.
100 *
101 * Compared case-insensitively, so a `Render/` authored on Windows is still recognized on Linux.

103[[nodiscard]] MOCHI_API bool IsAssetRoleSubdirName(std::string_view name);

105/**
106 * @brief Resolve the base folder of the asset that @p originDir belongs to.
107 *
108 * @details Ascends to the nearest role-folder ancestor (@ref IsAssetRoleSubdirName) and resolves to
109 * its parent; a path with no role folder above it resolves to itself. Nothing on disk is consulted.
110 *
111 * This anchors lookups and default save paths on the asset itself rather than on a fixed number of
112 * directory levels. Counting levels breaks on a flat asset, where it reaches past the asset into
113 * the folder holding its siblings -- a namespace shared with unrelated assets. Ascending rather
114 * than checking only the immediate name additionally handles a role folder partitioned into
115 * subfolders, e.g. `cad/internal/` holding CAD sources that must not be open-sourced.
116 *
117 * @warning Being purely lexical, this treats any role-folder name on the way up as the asset's,
118 * so an asset nested beneath a folder that happens to be named `cad` / `render` / `collision` /
119 * `intermediates` anchors one level too high. No asset in the tree is laid out that way.
120 *
121 * @param[in] originDir Directory holding the file being worked on.
122 *
123 * @return The asset's base folder.
124 */
125[[nodiscard]] MOCHI_API std::filesystem::path FindAssetBaseFolder(
126 std::filesystem::path const& originDir);
127
128/**
129 * @brief Classify the layout of the asset that @p originDir belongs to.
130 *
131 * @details @ref AssetFolderLayout::RoleSubdirs when @p originDir sits inside a role folder -- it is
132 * one, or a subfolder of one, so the asset demonstrably uses them -- or when the base folder
133 * already holds any role folder; @ref AssetFolderLayout::Flat otherwise. Only the second test
134 * touches the filesystem.
135 *
136 * @param[in] originDir Directory holding the file being worked on.
137 *
138 * @return The layout in use.
139 */
140[[nodiscard]] MOCHI_API AssetFolderLayout
141DetectAssetFolderLayout(std::filesystem::path const& originDir);
142
143/**
144 * @brief Directory that a newly written file of role @p roleSubdir belongs in, for a file being
145 * worked on in @p originDir.
146 *
147 * @details `<base>/<roleSubdir>` under @ref AssetFolderLayout::RoleSubdirs, whether or not that
148 * folder exists yet: exporting the render and collision models of a STEP opened from `cad/` fills
149 * `render/` and `collision/` rather than dropping them beside the STEP. The base folder itself
150 * under @ref AssetFolderLayout::Flat, which keeps a flat asset flat. Creating the directory is the
151 * caller's job (see @ref EnsureDirectoriesCreated).
152 *
153 * @note @ref kIntermediatesSubdir is the deliberate exception, and always yields
154 * `<base>/intermediates`: generated pipelines and scratch exports are bookkeeping rather than
155 * asset content, so they stay out of a flat asset's folder.
156 *
157 * @param[in] originDir Directory holding the file being worked on.
158 * @param[in] roleSubdir One of @ref kAssetRoleSubdirs. Empty yields the base folder.
159 *
160 * @return The directory to write into.
161 */
162[[nodiscard]] MOCHI_API std::filesystem::path AssetRoleFolderForWrite(
163 std::filesystem::path const& originDir,
164 std::string_view roleSubdir);

236/**
237 * @brief Parse a `.superdex_root` JSON file into its tag table.
238 *
239 * The file is a JSON object mapping `"@tagName"` keys to path strings.
240 * Empty or whitespace-only files are valid and produce an empty tag table.
241 * Relative tag values are resolved against the directory containing the
242 * `.superdex_root` file, then @c weakly_canonical-ized. Each resolved tag
243 * directory is verified to itself contain a `.superdex_root` marker.
244 *
245 * Any invalid entry (malformed key, key not matching the @ref kTagPrefix
246 * identifier rules, or target directory missing a `.superdex_root` marker)
247 * is treated as a hard error: the function logs the offending entry and returns
248 * failure with no tags loaded.
249 *
250 * @param[in] rootFilePath Path to the `.superdex_root` file.
251 * @param[in,out] error Error status. Check @ref Error::IsOK for success.
252 *
253 * @return Parsed tag table on success, default-constructed on failure.
254 */
255[[nodiscard]] MOCHI_API ParsedRootFile
256ParseRootFile(std::filesystem::path const& rootFilePath, superdex::Error& error);
257
258/**
259 * @brief Absolute + lexically normalized, with any trailing separator dropped.
260 *
261 * @details The single definition of what a bot path means, used wherever one is resolved, compared
262 * or collected. Symlinks are deliberately NOT resolved: an asset tree can be a symlink farm
263 * (buck-out file groups are), and resolving would place a file that exists in the link's target
264 * tree while a file the build does not have -- which a bot may legitimately name -- has no link to
265 * follow and stays where it was written. The two then have no relative form between them. Treating
266 * paths as written keeps every reference in one tree, at the cost of not recognising two spellings
267 * of one file as the same; an archive then carries such a file at both paths, which is what its
268 * references require.
269 *
270 * @param[in] path Path to normalize; may name a file that does not exist.
271 *
272 * @return Normalized absolute path.
273 */
274[[nodiscard]] MOCHI_API std::filesystem::path NormalizeBotPath(std::filesystem::path const& path);
275
276/**
277 * @brief Resolve a bot path string into an absolute path.
278 *
279 * The single source of truth for path resolution rules used by all bot
280 * file references:
281 * - Empty input -> empty result.
282 * - A file-relative @p input may ascend at most @p maxParentDepth parent
283 * (`..`) directories; more than that -> hard error. `@tag/...` and
284 * `//...` remainders are always descendant-only (any `..` -> hard error),
285 * regardless of @p maxParentDepth.
286 * - Absolute input -> hard error (absolute bot paths are not allowed).
287 * - `@tag/...` -> look up `@tag` in the nearest `.superdex_root` tag
288 * table (walking up from @p basePath) and join the remainder.
289 * - `//...` -> resolve against the directory of the nearest
290 * `.superdex_root` marker (regardless of its tag table).
291 * - Anything else -> join with @p basePath.parent_path() and
292 * @c weakly_canonical.
293 *
294 * @param[in] input Raw path string (e.g. from a `.superdex_bot` or .mochi_bot_scene field).
295 * @param[in] basePath The referencing file (its parent directory is used as
296 * the search/join origin).
297 * @param[in] maxParentDepth Maximum number of parent (`..`) directories a file-relative path may
298 * ascend. Pass @c 0 for descendant-only, which all bot references use. Callers
299 * that store loosely-coupled local clusters (e.g. Studio's
300 * `.StudioProcessing.json`) may pass a small positive value. No default: every
301 * caller must state its policy explicitly.
302 * @param[in,out] error Error status. Check @ref Error::IsOK for success.
303 *
304 * @return Absolute resolved path.
305 */
306[[nodiscard]] MOCHI_API std::filesystem::path ResolveBotPath(
307 std::string_view input,
308 std::filesystem::path const& basePath,
309 int maxParentDepth,
310 superdex::Error& error);
311
312/**
313 * @brief Convert an absolute path to its canonical bot-path string form for serialization.
314 *
315 * This is the inverse of @ref ResolveBotPath.
316 *
317 * The result is always a valid @ref ResolveBotPath input that resolves to the
318 * same absolute path. It is **not** guaranteed to be string-identical to the
319 * original input, because multiple input forms may refer to the same path and
320 * this function deterministically selects the highest-priority form per the
321 * rules below. For example, an input `@assets/foo` whose target is also
322 * reachable via `//` will round-trip as `//foo`.
323 *
324 * Selection rules, applied in order:
325 * 1. File-relative — if @p absPath is reachable from @c basePath.parent_path()
326 * while ascending at most @p maxParentDepth parent (`..`) directories, emit
327 * that relative form. With the default @p maxParentDepth of @c 0 this is a
328 * plain descendant, as all bot references require.
329 * 2. `//root-prefixed` — else, if @p absPath is a descendant of @c FindBotsRoot(basePath),
330 * emit `//+remainder` (always descendant-only).
331 * 3. `@tag/...` — else, parse the nearest `.superdex_root` tag table and pick
332 * the tag whose target directory is the deepest (most path components) strict
333 * ancestor of @p absPath; ties are broken by lexicographically smallest tag name;
334 * emit `@tag/+remainder` (always descendant-only).
335 *
336 * If none of the above produce a valid relative form, the function reports a
337 * hard error: absolute bot paths are not permitted on either end of resolution.
338 *
339 * Empty input -> empty result. Already-relative input is returned unchanged
340 * (defensive; should not happen post-load).
341 *
342 * @param[in] absPath Absolute path to convert.
343 * @param[in] basePath The referencing file (its parent directory and bots-root context
344 * determine the chosen prefix form).
345 * @param[in] maxParentDepth Maximum number of parent (`..`) directories the file-relative
346 * form (rule 1) may ascend before falling back to `//` / `@tag`. Pass @c 0
347 * for descendant-only, which all bot references use. The `//` and `@tag`
348 * forms are unaffected and stay descendant-only. No default: every caller must
349 * state its policy explicitly.
350 * @param[in,out] error Error status. Check @ref Error::IsOK for success.
351 *
352 * @return Canonical string representation acceptable as @ref ResolveBotPath input.
353 */
354[[nodiscard]] MOCHI_API DynamicString UnresolveBotPath(
355 std::filesystem::path const& absPath,
356 std::filesystem::path const& basePath,
357 int maxParentDepth,
358 superdex::Error& error);
359

599// Geometry (URDF and MJCF)

601
602/* @brief Geometry types of URDF and MJCF geoms. URDF has only spheres, cylinders, boxes, and
603 * meshes. */
604enum class GeomType { Plane, Hfield, Sphere, Capsule, Ellipsoid, Cylinder, Box, Mesh, Sdf };
605
606/* @brief True for the primitive geom types: sphere, capsule, ellipsoid, cylinder, and box. */
607constexpr bool IsPrimitiveGeom(GeomType type) {
608 return type == GeomType::Sphere || type == GeomType::Capsule || type == GeomType::Ellipsoid ||
609 type == GeomType::Cylinder || type == GeomType::Box;
610}
611
612/* @brief One visual or collision geometry of a link: an MJCF `<geom>` (resolved against its default
613 * class and assets), or a URDF `<visual>` or `<collision>`.
614 *
615 * @details Poses are expressed in the frame of the link that holds the geom. Mesh vertices map into
616 * that frame as `linkFromGeom * geomFromMesh * (meshScale * v)`. Fields marked MJCF keep their
617 * defaults for URDF. */
618struct GeomReference {
619 /* @brief Geom name, or empty if unnamed. */
620 DynamicString name;
621 /* @brief Geom type. */
622 GeomType type = GeomType::Sphere;
623 /* @brief Primitive size, in MuJoCo's convention (for MJCF, after resolving `fromto`). Sphere:
624 * radius. Capsule and cylinder: radius, half-length. Ellipsoid: radii. Box: half-extents. Unused
625 * for meshes, and for MJCF primitives that name a mesh, which MuJoCo fits to that mesh instead
626 * (see @ref fitScale). [m] */
627 Real3 size = {};
628 /* @brief Geom pose in the link frame. */
629 TransformRT linkFromGeom;
630 /* @brief Mesh file reference verbatim (MJCF mesh `file`, URDF mesh `filename`), or empty for
631 * geoms that name no mesh. */
632 DynamicString meshRef;
633 /* @brief Resolved mesh path on disk, or empty if the mesh is missing or the geom names none. */
634 DynamicString meshFile;
635 /* @brief MJCF `fitscale` of a primitive that names a mesh. MuJoCo sizes such a primitive to the
636 * mesh's equivalent-inertia box, scaled by this factor, and centers it on the mesh's principal
637 * frame; the loader leaves the fitting to callers that load the mesh. */
638 real fitScale = 1_r;
639 /* @brief Mesh `scale`. */
640 Real3 meshScale = {1_r, 1_r, 1_r};
641 /* @brief Mesh vertices in the geom frame, from the MJCF mesh `refpos` / `refquat`. */
642 TransformRT geomFromMesh;
643 /* @brief Color. MJCF: the geom `rgba`, else its material, else MuJoCo's default gray. URDF: the
644 * material color. */
645 Real4 rgba = {0.5_r, 0.5_r, 0.5_r, 1_r};
646 /* @brief True if the geom has a color or texture of its own (MJCF: a material or explicit
647 * `rgba`; URDF: a material with a color or texture). */
648 bool hasMaterial = false;
649 /* @brief If true, a mesh file with materials of its own (DAE, GLB, or OBJ with a material
650 * library) keeps them, and the geom's color and texture apply only to meshes without (URDF, as
651 * RViz renders). If false, they replace the mesh's materials (MJCF). */
652 bool keepMeshMaterials = false;
653 /* @brief Resolved 2D texture image of the geom's material, or empty. */
654 DynamicString textureFile;
655 /* @brief MJCF material `texrepeat`. */
656 std::array<real, 2> texRepeat = {1_r, 1_r};
657 /* @brief MJCF material `shininess`, in [0, 1]. */
658 real shininess = 0.5_r;
659 /* @brief Explicit MJCF geom `mass` [kg], if set. */
660 std::optional<real> mass;
661 /* @brief Explicit MJCF geom `density` [kg/m^3], if set. */
662 std::optional<real> density;
663 /* @brief MJCF sliding friction coefficient (first `friction` component), if set. */
664 std::optional<real> friction;
665 /* @brief MJCF contact bitmasks. */
666 int contype = 1;
667 int conaffinity = 1;
668 /* @brief MJCF visibility group. */
669 int group = 0;
670 /* @brief True if the geom participates in contact: a URDF `<collision>`, or an MJCF geom whose
671 * `contype | conaffinity` is nonzero. */
672 bool isCollision = true;
673 /* @brief True if the geom is rendered: a URDF `<visual>`, or an MJCF geom that MuJoCo renders
674 * by default (group 0-2 and not fully transparent). */
675 bool isVisual = true;
676 /* @brief File to use as this geom's Mochi shape. The loaders set it to @ref meshFile for mesh
677 * geoms and leave it empty for primitives; callers that generate primitive shapes fill it in
678 * before calling @ref ExpandUrdfGeomLinks or @ref ExpandMjcfGeomLinks. */
679 DynamicString shapeFile;
680 /* @brief File to use as this geom's render model, set like @ref shapeFile. */
681 DynamicString renderModelFile;
682};

960#if MOCHI_USE_REFLECTION
961
962/**
963 * @brief Load an SReflect-annotated struct from a JSON file.
964 *
965 * By default (strict mode), any issue reported by the deserializer —
966 * unrecognized keys, missing keys — is treated as an error. Pass
967 * @p allowPartial = true to permit partial loads where missing fields
968 * retain their C++ default values.
969 *
970 * @tparam T The struct type (must have MOCHI_STRUCT_BEGIN/END macros).
971 * @param[in] path Path to the JSON file.
972 * @param[in,out] error Error status.
973 * @param[in] allowPartial If true, permit partial loads (missing fields keep defaults).
974 * @return Loaded struct, or default-constructed on failure.
975 */
976template <typename T>
977T LoadParamsFromFile(std::string_view path, superdex::Error& error, bool allowPartial = false) {
978 MOCHI_ERROR_RETURN(error, {});
979 T params;
980 int numIssues = 0;
981 std::string pathStr(path);
982 bool const success = SReflect::LoadFromJsonFile(
983 params, pathStr.c_str(), SReflect::DeserializeFlags::Default, numIssues);
984 MOCHI_ERROR_IF(!success, error, "Failed to load params from file");
985 MOCHI_ERROR_RETURN(error, {});
986 if (!allowPartial) {
987 MOCHI_ERROR_IF(numIssues > 0, error, "Params file has issues (unrecognized or missing fields)");
988 MOCHI_ERROR_RETURN(error, {});
989 }
990 return params;
991}
992
993/**
994 * @brief True if @p value looks like inline JSON -- its first non-whitespace character is '{' or
995 * '[' -- rather than a path to a JSON file. Empty / all-whitespace returns false.
996 */
997[[nodiscard]] MOCHI_API bool IsInlineJson(std::string_view value);
998
999/**
1000 * @brief Load an SReflect-annotated struct from a value that is EITHER a path to a JSON file OR an
1001 * inline JSON string. Inline JSON is detected via @ref IsInlineJson; any other non-empty value is
1002 * treated as a file path (a .json/.superdex_* file). An empty value yields a default-constructed
1003 * struct. Same strict / @p allowPartial semantics as @ref LoadParamsFromFile.
1004 *
1005 * Sensors, controllers, and (future) actuators use this so a scene/bot entry's params or initArgs
1006 * may be given either as a path or inline JSON. When @p outBaseDir is non-null it receives the
1007 * directory against which relative paths the struct itself references (e.g. a model/weights file)
1008 * should be resolved: the params file's parent directory in the path case, or empty in the inline
1009 * case (inline JSON has no base directory, so any paths it references must be absolute).
1010 *
1011 * @tparam T The struct type (must have MOCHI_STRUCT_BEGIN/END macros).
1012 * @param[in] pathOrJson A file path, an inline JSON string, or empty.
1013 * @param[in,out] error Error status.
1014 * @param[in] allowPartial If true, permit partial loads (missing fields keep defaults).
1015 * @param[out] outBaseDir Optional base directory for resolving relative sub-paths (see above).
1016 * @return Loaded struct, or default-constructed on failure / empty input.
1017 */
1018template <typename T>
1019T LoadParamsFromPathOrJson(
1020 std::string_view pathOrJson,
1021 superdex::Error& error,
1022 bool allowPartial = false,
1023 std::string* outBaseDir = nullptr) {
1024 MOCHI_ERROR_RETURN(error, {});
1025 if (outBaseDir != nullptr) {
1026 outBaseDir->clear();
1027 }
1028 T params;
1029 if (pathOrJson.empty()) {
1030 return params;
1031 }
1032 int numIssues = 0;
1033 if (IsInlineJson(pathOrJson)) {
1034 // The numIssues overload of FromJsonString returns void; a malformed JSON string surfaces as
1035 // numIssues > 0 (caught by the strict check below unless allowPartial).
1036 SReflect::FromJsonString(
1037 params, std::string(pathOrJson), SReflect::DeserializeFlags::Default, numIssues);
1038 } else {
1039 std::string const pathStr(pathOrJson);
1040 bool const success = SReflect::LoadFromJsonFile(
1041 params, pathStr.c_str(), SReflect::DeserializeFlags::Default, numIssues);
1042 MOCHI_ERROR_IF(!success, error, "Failed to load params from file");
1043 MOCHI_ERROR_RETURN(error, {});
1044 if (outBaseDir != nullptr) {
1045 *outBaseDir = std::filesystem::path(pathStr).parent_path().string();
1046 }
1047 }
1048 if (!allowPartial) {
1049 MOCHI_ERROR_IF(numIssues > 0, error, "Params have issues (unrecognized or missing fields)");
1050 MOCHI_ERROR_RETURN(error, {});
1051 }
1052 return params;
1053}
1054
1055/**
1056 * @brief Save an SReflect-annotated struct to a JSON file.
1057 * @tparam T The struct type (must have MOCHI_STRUCT_BEGIN/END macros).
1058 * @param[in] params The struct to serialize.
1059 * @param[in] path Destination file path.
1060 * @param[in,out] error Error status.
1061 */
1062template <typename T>
1063void SaveParamsToFile(T const& params, std::string_view path, superdex::Error& error) {
1064 MOCHI_ERROR_RETURN(error);
1065 std::string pathStr(path);
1066 bool const success = SReflect::SaveToJsonFile(params, pathStr.c_str());
1067 MOCHI_ERROR_IF(!success, error, "Failed to save params to file");
1068}
1069
1070#endif // MOCHI_USE_REFLECTION
